MC	<p>b22e_51c1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fk, ++, fk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #266294;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #266294;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266294;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a3356;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9a3356;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>ae20_aeda</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8f4717;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3357b8;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3357b8;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>6020_90e4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5d641a;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5d641a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5d641a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a3356;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9a3356;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5f48b4;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #5f48b4;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>99f8_0f8a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c06;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #715c06;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c06;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8c3a7a;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hx, ++, hx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c85b_e34b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3e6b29;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3e6b29;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3e6b29;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3357b8;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3357b8;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3357b8;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, be, ++, be"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8886_a1e9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>41b8_ab08</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #226d49;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #226d49;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #226d49;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a3356;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9a3356;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #066885;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #066885;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>5157_5024</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5d641a;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5d641a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5d641a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a3356;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9a3356;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d736_9cf1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8f4717;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #066885;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #066885;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #066885;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hx, ++, hx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>e39a_ce10</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f4717;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #226d49;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #226d49;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #226d49;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kp, ++, kp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>aa8b_84c3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f4717;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #226d49;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #226d49;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #226d49;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fk, ++, fk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c06;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #715c06;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d96f_5542</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8f4717;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3357b8;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3357b8;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3357b8;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mp, ++, mp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">4,800</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> MC	<p>df2f_1b1d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c06;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #715c06;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c06;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #715c06;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c06;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3357b8;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3357b8;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>ad09_866f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5d641a;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5d641a;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5d641a;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f36a6;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7f36a6;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f36a6;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, aw, ++, aw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3d20_1bde</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f36a6;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7f36a6;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>7533_d541</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8f4717;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266294;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #266294;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f4717;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5f48b4;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #5f48b4;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>434e_3ecc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006b73;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006b73;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b73;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8c3a7a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3a7a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dk, ++, dk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>687c_22d8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8f4717;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3357b8;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3357b8;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #226d49;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #226d49;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>1bba_78d0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, at, ++, at"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8290_9f32</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266294;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #266294;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f36a6;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7f36a6;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>aba6_c123</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8f4717;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3357b8;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3357b8;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3357b8;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, tw, ++, tw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9584_1a6b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13128;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a13128;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13128;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #066885;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #066885;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>10a6_6774</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13128;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a13128;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13128;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3357b8;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3357b8;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>03e0_9b19</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3e6b29;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3e6b29;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3e6b29;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266294;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #266294;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266294;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fm, ++, fm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2db9_3cdc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d61;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5f48b4;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5f48b4;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8f4717;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>9808_264c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13128;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a13128;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13128;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266294;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #266294;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266294;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bc, ++, bc"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5d641a;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5d641a;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5d641a;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3357b8;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3357b8;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>63d9_9db0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13128;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a13128;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13128;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266294;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #266294;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266294;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, jm, ++, jm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7021_eddb</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #715c06;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #715c06;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #715c06;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b73;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006b73;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b73;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ty, ++, ty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d61;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006d61;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>5e25_89f3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266294;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #266294;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>a531_4a39</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #226d49;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #226d49;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #226d49;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5f48b4;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5f48b4;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5f48b4;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fh, ++, fh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8f4717;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f4717;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #066885;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #066885;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>ecc0_3b92</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5d641a;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5d641a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5d641a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a3356;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9a3356;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a3356;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hr, ++, hr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0d70_4556</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3e6b29;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3e6b29;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3e6b29;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5f48b4;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #5f48b4;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3e6b29;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3e6b29;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3e6b29;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f36a6;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7f36a6;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>2b6a_ca56</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #825200;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #825200;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #825200;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f36a6;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7f36a6;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype.
